transcript.answer: No, not any more. ADR-039 originally decided that review-type agents should run on a different model family from the implementer. The settings UI would warn when both resolved to the same family. PR #1091 added the helpers for that warning. The ADR's amendment dated 2026-10-14 reversed this. `code-review` and `code-review-recheck` now run on `gemini-4-argon`, the same family as the implementation loop's `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. `code-review-reply` stays on `claude-sonnet-4-6`. The amendment says that a bench on five merged PRs showed a better catch rate for Argon. That outweighed the self-preference risk, so cross-family review is no longer a rule. It is now only one input to the model choice. The cost is that Argon is about 3x slower and about 40% dearer.

judgements.reason: The answer says ADR-039 'decided' cross-family review and that it is 'no longer a rule', but the gold says the ADR is still a draft and was never a rule, even though the answer's final 'No' and its amendment details match.
